_comment: Tier-2 for sparta rarefied_flow: compute thermal/grid across an unresolved velocity gradient — the effect is real and it is nothing like the size the entry implies. Six decks were run on the installed binary (SPARTA 24 Sep 2025, spa_serial): a Couette slab of argon between two diffuse walls at the same temperature translating at -1000 and +1000 m/s, well above the thermal speed, on a 4-cell and a 40-cell grid, three seeds each. TWO CONFOUNDS had to be removed first, and an earlier attempt at this claim was abandoned over the first. rarefied_flow:6's low-occupancy bias pushes the cell-average DOWN and refining the grid lowers occupancy, so it acts in the same direction as the effect under test; everything here is read through 'fix ave/grid', which the thermal_grid_is_biased_low_at_few_particles fixture establishes removes that bias at every resolution (occupancy here falls 1250 -> 12.5 across the refinement). And because a DSMC cell average is stochastic, each grid is run on three seeds and the question asked is whether the two CLUSTERS separate rather than whether two numbers differ. CORRECTED: the entry said the temperature 'FALLS SUBSTANTIALLY when you refine the grid' and offered that as the test. Measured, the fall is 4.6 percent — coarse 1153.8/1161.6/1170.1 against fine 1106.6/1110.5/1109.8, no overlap between the clusters and about three times the coarse seed spread, so it is real and resolvable, but an agent told to look for a substantial fall would not recognise four percent as the signal and on a single seed pair it is only a few times the noise. The magnitude follows from the mechanism: the sub-cell velocity spread is (dU/dy)*dy, so its variance enters as the SQUARE of the cell size and in only one of three velocity components. The entry now states that. No temperature is pinned; the assertions are the cluster separation, the drop measured against the seed spread, and an upper bound that encodes the correction. COVERS: rarefied_flow:5. MUTATION CONTROL (added 2026-08-06, re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 zeroes BOTH wall translation velocities, leaving grids, seeds, occupancy, wall temperature and run length identical -- it removes the velocity gradient, which is the entire mechanism. Measured against the noise floor rather than a fixed tolerance: the coarse-to-fine drop collapses from 0.04552 (4.55 percent, coarse seed spread 0.01403) to 0.005372 (0.54 percent, coarse seed spread 0.01261), i.e. the signal lands BELOW the independently measured seed spread, and the coarse and fine clusters stop separating (coarse [273.851, 272.628, 270.419] now overlaps fine [270.521, 270.833, 271.156]). This is deliberately not a reseed or a shortened run: perturbing a stochastic run proves nothing, landing the signal on the measured floor proves the fixture responds to the shear. Verified: unmutated the fixture PASSES (rc=0); with T2_MUTATE=1 it FAILS (rc=1) and these expect_in_output strings go False and disappear: refining_lowers_the_reading_on_every_seed_pairing=True, the_effect_is_resolvable_above_the_seed_spread=True. Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/sparta/thermal_grid_across_an_unresolved_shear && python source.py (passes, rc=0), then T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py (fails, rc=1). Needs a SPARTA binary: the fixtures find spa_serial/spa_mpi on PATH or at ~/Schreibtisch/sparta/src/spa_serial, else set SPARTA_BINARY; with none present they exit 0 on a SKIP: line.
